title: Microsoft Teams: allowed list of external meeting notetaker bots
summary: Hold: the briefing assumes existing behaviour continues until an administrator acts, although Microsoft has not stated the new control's default. It also labels the planned list tenant-scoped without evidence of its configuration scope. The roadmap facts and the existing meeting-policy path and PowerShell command are supported.

claims.claim: Teams plans an administrator-configured list of external meeting bots allowed to join meetings hosted in the organisation.
claims.quote: Admins will be able to configure a list of external meeting bots which are allowed to join meetings hosted in their organization.

claims.quote: or let them be enforced into the currently available high friction lobby experience.

claims.quote: The allowed bots will be treated like a regular external participant to the meeting

claims.quote: and meeting policies will be enforced as appropriate.

claims.claim: No admin UI setting or API for the planned allowed-bots list is documented in November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams allowed external meeting notetaker bots list PowerShell Microsoft Graph allowlist configuration admin setting. Read manage-external-bots, Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy and searched graph/utcm-teams-resources for bot/list settings; no named-list control.

claims.claim: The planned allowed-bots list is a tenant-scoped configuration control.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams external bots allow list default policy scope bot identity Bot Identification Program BlockDetectedBots override blocked participants. The roadmap describes hosted meetings, not assignment scope; manage-external-bots documents scope only for the existing policy.
claims.fix: Set controls[0].scope to 'other' and add to its note: 'The configuration and assignment scope of the planned list is not yet documented.' Hosting meetings in the organisation does not establish tenant-wide configuration scope.

claims.quote: Searched: Teams external bots allow list default policy scope bot identity Bot Identification Program BlockDetectedBots override blocked participants. Read the roadmap, manage-external-bots and teams-bot-identification; only the existing detection policy has a stated default.

claims.claim: Today's documented behaviour continues until an administrator acts on the new list.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams external bots allow list default policy scope bot identity Bot Identification Program BlockDetectedBots override blocked participants. Read roadmap, manage-external-bots and teams-bot-identification; none states that the new list waits for administrator action.
claims.fix: Replace the paragraph's first sentence with: 'Microsoft has not stated what happens on arrival, and no source says existing behaviour will change; this briefing therefore treats the list as a decision for security and Teams owners rather than a deadline.' Keep defaultState as 'unknown'.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a required administrator action for the planned list.

claims.claim: The existing Teams bot detection mechanism uses signals collected during the meeting join process.
claims.quote: Teams uses built-in detection mechanisms to identify external AI bots based on signals collected during the meeting join process.

claims.claim: With bot detection enabled, detected bots are placed in the lobby regardless of the meeting's lobby configuration.
claims.quote: When bot detection is enabled, meeting organizers see enhanced controls and visibility. The participants detected as bots are placed in the meeting lobby irrespective of the lobby configuration for the meeting.

claims.claim: Detected bots require explicit admission under the existing approval setting.
claims.quote: Bots are detected and marked in the lobby. They're enforced to be in the lobby until explicitly admitted into the meeting.

claims.claim: The external-bots guide says presenters can admit detected bots depending on the meeting setting.
claims.quote: Organizers (also presenters, depending on the meeting setting), need to explicitly admit these bots into the meeting.
claims.fix: Add after the sentence about presenters: 'The Teams Bot Identification Program page instead describes detected bots as requiring organizer approval before joining (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/teams-bot-identification).' This reports the different wording in the two cited pages.

claims.claim: When detected, require approval before joining, represented by RequireApprovalWhenDetected, is the existing setting's default.
claims.quote: | When detected, require approval before joining | *RequireApprovalWhenDetected* | (**default**) Bots are detected and marked in the lobby.

claims.where: Why it matters; controls[1].note; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The external-bots guide also lists Do not detect bots as an option.
claims.quote: | Do not detect bots | *AllowBots* | Bots aren't detected or marked in the lobby or in the meeting. They appear as any other external participant in the meetings. |

claims.claim: The Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy reference additionally documents BlockDetectedBots to block detected external bots.
claims.quote: BlockDetectedBots: When detected, external third-party meeting bots and meeting assistants are blocked from joining meetings hosted in the organization.

claims.claim: External notetaker bots may record or transcribe meetings without participant awareness.
claims.quote: These bots may: Record or transcribe meetings without participant awareness.

claims.claim: External bots may store meeting data in third-party systems outside the organisation's compliance boundaries.
claims.quote: Store meeting data in third-party systems outside of the organization's compliance boundaries.

claims.claim: Some external bots may not be detected by the existing mechanism.
claims.quote: Some external bots may not be detected. We're constantly improving our detection mechanism and filling in any gaps that are observed.

claims.claim: The roadmap does not say whether the new list depends on existing bot detection.
claims.quote: Admins will be able to configure a list of external meeting bots which are allowed to join meetings hosted in their organization.

claims.claim: The Teams Bot Identification Program is described as a public preview for independent software vendors.
claims.quote: Microsoft Teams Bot Identification Program (Public Preview). Microsoft is also introducing the Teams Bot Identification Program to support independent software vendors (ISVs) that build meeting bot experiences for Teams.

claims.claim: Eligible bot providers can register with Microsoft through the Bot Identification Program.
claims.quote: Through this program, eligible bot providers can register with Microsoft

claims.claim: Registered bot providers can include a self-identification marker in their meeting join requests.
claims.quote: and include a self-identification marker in their meeting join requests. When Teams recognizes this marker, it can identify the bot as a registered participant.

claims.quote: Searched: Teams external bots allow list default policy scope bot identity Bot Identification Program BlockDetectedBots override blocked participants. Opened teams-bot-identification and manage-external-bots; neither connects registration to a named allow list.

claims.claim: The roadmap does not describe transcript-storage restrictions for allowed bots.
claims.quote: The allowed bots will be treated like a regular external participant to the meeting and meeting policies will be enforced as appropriate.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes bot entry controls and does not document new access beyond regular external participation.
claims.quote: The allowed bots will be treated like a regular external participant to the meeting and meeting policies will be enforced as appropriate.

claims.claim: Detection may occasionally misclassify human participants as bots.
claims.quote: Detection may occasionally misclassify human participants as bots.

claims.claim: Misclassified participants can be admitted from the lobby and marked This is not a bot.
claims.quote: you can rectify the situation by admitting the participants from the lobby and marking them with "This is not a bot" option.

claims.quote: Searched: Teams external bots allow list default policy scope bot identity Bot Identification Program BlockDetectedBots override blocked participants. Read manage-external-bots and Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy; lobby correction is described, but no override of the planned list's block.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -ExternalBotAccessMode RequireApprovalWhenDetected sets the existing bot approval policy.
claims.quote: RequireApprovalWhenDetected: When detected, bots will be enforced to the meeting lobby, regardless of the lobby setting of the meeting. They will require approval before getting access to the meetings. This is the default value.

claims.claim: The existing detection setting is not documented as a way to approve named bots.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams allowed external meeting notetaker bots list PowerShell Microsoft Graph allowlist configuration admin setting. Read manage-external-bots and ExternalBotAccessMode in Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy; their options control detection, approval or blocking, not named approvals.

claims.claim: The external-bots page does not state the administrator role required to edit meeting policies.
